The next generation of iPhone is coming, and it's going to be a little different. The base iPhone 18 won't be making an appearance for now, as that model has been moved to a spring launch. This September's headliners will be the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone 18 Pro Max, and an all-new foldable iPhone.

Of course, there's an elephant in the room: the price hike. An increase for the iPhone 18 Pro lineup is virtually inevitable, which raises the question — does it make sense to buy an iPhone 17 Pro at current prices?

What's new in iPhone 18 Pro

The iPhone 18 Pro is a modest upgrade over the iPhone 17 Pro, but I wouldn't call it an "S year."

Key new features include a smaller Dynamic Island, a main camera with a variable aperture for finer depth-of-field control, a fresh lineup of color options (including a red model), and Apple's first C2 modem in a Pro iPhone, which also supports satellite 5G connectivity.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max will be thicker with a larger battery, and paired with the C2 modem, that should translate to a solid boost in battery life.

There's a routine chip upgrade coming in the A20 Pro (one of the first 2nm chips) and the N2 networking chip. The iPhone 18 Pro is expected to retain the same 12GB of RAM as the previous generation. Apple will also redesign the Camera Control button to reduce accidental triggers.

Apple will likely have more surprise upgrades in store, but that's what's known so far.

The price hike problem

This is the most controversial point. Apple has already raised prices significantly across its iPad and Mac lines, and has warned that more increases are on the way. A price hike for the iPhone 18 Pro lineup is almost a given.

How much? That's the hard part to pin down. Estimates have suggested as much as a $300 increase, though Apple could also opt for a more modest bump and absorb some of the cost itself. I expect the base iPhone 18 Pro to land somewhere between $1,199 and $1,399, and the iPhone 18 Pro Max between $1,299 and $1,499.

For most people, this would be a hard-to-swallow increase, especially when the new iPhone doesn't bring a significant enough feature boost to justify it.

Should you buy now?

Of course, it all depends on you. Personally, I think the iPhone 17 Pro will offer a smartphone experience roughly on par with the iPhone 18 Pro, at a lower price. It's a hard argument to counter.

Apple hasn't raised iPhone prices yet, so today you can still grab the iPhone 17 Pro for $1,099, or the iPhone 17 Pro Max for $1,199. If you're on an older iPhone and thinking of upgrading, even at the tail end of the cycle, last year's model is still the smartest buy.

The memory shortage caused by AI data centers is expected to persist for years, so Apple prices aren't likely to come down anytime soon. Plan accordingly.

  • Anker MagSafe/Qi2 ultra-slim portable battery
  • AirPods Pro 3 (twice the noise cancellation of the AirPods Pro 2!)
  • Anker Nano 45W smart display fast charger
  • Anker Nano 13-in-1 MacBook dock
  • Logitech MX Master 4 Mac edition mouse
  • Belkin Qi2 3-in-1 MagSafe charging stand
